stem: A 6-year-old boy is found to have leukopaenia on a full blood count after several days of fever and coryza; which additional laboratory pattern would be most concerning for broader marrow involvement rather than an isolated issue?

options.text: An isolated low neutrophil count with other cell lines preserved
A second low cell line such as thrombocytopaenia in addition to the leukopaenia
A white cell abnormality interpreted without reference to the other blood cell lines
A single abnormal white cell result assessed without considering bicytopaenia or pancytopaenia
A leukopaenia pattern assumed to be unimportant because white counts vary with age

explanation: Broader marrow involvement is suggested by bicytopaenia or pancytopaenia. A low white cell count together with another low cell line, such as thrombocytopaenia, is more concerning than an isolated leukopaenia.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: WBC Disorders

rationale: The key distinction is whether only one blood cell line is affected or whether multiple cell lines are reduced. More than one low cell line raises concern for a marrow process rather than an isolated white cell abnormality.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because an isolated neutrophil reduction does not by itself indicate broader multi-line marrow involvement.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because leukopaenia plus another low cell line, such as thrombocytopaenia, suggests bicytopaenia and possible broader marrow involvement.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because this is an incomplete interpretation rather than the concerning laboratory pattern itself.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the important issue is whether more than one cell line is low, not simply that the white cell result is abnormal.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because age-related variation may affect interpretation, but it does not make leukopaenia reassuring when another cell line is also low.
